title: Request for Increased Overhead Stowage Volume on the ZEPHYR-18 Sub-Fleet
abstract: Operator asks for the larger overhead stowage compartments of the later cabin standard to be made available on its two remaining ZEPHYR-18 aircraft. The request was assessed and declined on business grounds.

sections.request: Our passengers compare our ZEPHYR-18 rotations directly with the ZEPHYR-22 rotations on the same routes and the difference in bag space is the single most common complaint we receive. On the ZEPHYR-18 we are gate-checking roughly one bag in six on a full flight, which costs us turnaround time we do not have on a thirty-five minute schedule. We would like the deeper overhead bins that are standard on the rest of the family to be made available for our two ZEPHYR-18 aircraft, together with whatever ceiling and lighting rework that needs. We understand the aircraft are old and we are not asking for a full cabin refresh, only for the bins and the associated ceiling panels.
sections.background: The two aircraft were delivered in 2003 and 2017 and carry the original cabin standard. The operator raised the same request informally in 2024 and was told that no cross-programme bin solution existed for the shorter fuselage. Load factors on the affected routes average 93 per cent and the operator has no plans to retire either aircraft before 2031.
sections.expected_outcome: Availability of the current deeper overhead stowage standard for the ZEPHYR-18 fuselage, with an installation that can be completed in a single night stop per aircraft and that does not require re-certification of the emergency lighting or the oxygen distribution.

type_data.business_justification: Gate-checking of one bag in six on full ZEPHYR-18 rotations is estimated to cost the operator four minutes of turnaround per sector. The non-recurring cost of qualifying the deeper bin geometry for the shorter fuselage could not be recovered over a two-aircraft population, and the request was closed with a recommendation to revisit it only if a wider ZEPHYR-18 cabin programme is launched.
type_data.closure_note: Declined in June 2026. The deeper overhead stowage geometry has never been qualified for the shorter ZEPHYR-18 fuselage, and the ceiling, oxygen distribution and emergency lighting rework it would drag with it puts the non-recurring cost well beyond what a two-aircraft population can carry. The operator was offered a bin insert and a revised boarding procedure instead, and was told that the request would be reopened only if a wider ZEPHYR-18 cabin programme is launched.
